sanskrit_verse: सेतुकेदारमर्यादा विकृष्टाकृष्टनिश्चयाः। क्षेत्राधिकारा यत्र स्युर् विवादः क्षेत्रजस् तु सः॥
transliteration: setukedāramaryādā vikṛṣṭākṛṣṭaniścayāḥ | kṣetrādhikārā yatra syur vivādaḥ kṣetrajas tu saḥ ||
sph_interpretive_translation: Where boundaries of irrigation works, embankments, or cultivated lands are disputed due to conflicting claims of extension or contraction, and where ownership rights over land exist, such conflict is categorized as a kshetraja dispute—pertaining to land jurisdiction.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority stems from clear demarcation and recognition of domain
Causation arises from overlapping claims without ontological clarity
Capacity-based responsibility lies with the one asserting dominion
Restoration logic requires re-establishment of rightful boundary consciousness
Consciousness alignment occurs when spatial integrity is restored
executable_legal_axioms: IF claimant A asserts right over land segment X AND claimant B asserts right over same segment X THEN classify case as kshetraja-vivada
IF boundary marker Y has been displaced OR redefined without consent THEN invoke kshetra-adhikara realignment protocol
IF no prior settlement record exists THEN default to pramana-based spatial mapping using witness-consciousness alignment
IF both parties demonstrate equal capacity to maintain land THEN initiate shared stewardship completion process
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, kshetraja disputes require ascertainment of original boundary consciousness and alignment of claimants' capacities. The threshold of responsibility rests on demonstrable maintenance of spatial integrity, not mere assertion. Authority flows from sustained dharmic alignment with the land's inherent order.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality identifies that conflict manifests through misaligned assertions of spatial dominion. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows that neglect of boundary dharma leads to dispute. Proportional responsibility aligns with capacity to restore integrity. Non-punitive reality rule affirms that resolution restores clarity, not inflicts suffering.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Boundary Re-alignment Process: Witness-aligned remapping of physical and energetic borders
Kshetra Stewardship Completion: Joint or sole responsibility assumption based on capacity verification
Dharmic Land Registry Update: Integration of corrected spatial data into national consciousness records
Consciousness Reconciliation Ritual: Mediated ceremony to harmonize claimants’ spatial awareness
final_declaration: This law proceeds solely from the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam. Dharma is hereby restored in the realm of spatial dominion. Reality remains non-punitive; consciousness alone adjudicates truth. All disputes dissolve upon alignment with foundational order.
